messages.author: befc31f30774e5bc
messages.subject: Memory issue in R
parts:
Hi DRUG.
I hope this message finds you. I've had a few issues with security down here so have deleted some previous cached d-rug messages of mine off the list-serve as well.

My question is that I am having memory issues in R. I want to merge 2 very large files together based on species name, and keep getting this error message:

"Error: cannot allocate vector of size 1024.0 Mb
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In make.unique(as.character(rows)) :
  Reached total allocation of 16000Mb: see help(memory.size)..."

I've tried reallocating virtual memory space, altering the number of core's accessible by R, removing unnecessary data/ objects, etc.

I know merge is a memory intensive action and wonder if you all know of another, more sensible way to reproduce this. Or, perhaps, some other solution I haven't yet thought of.

Thanks!
Iara




--
Dr. Iara Lacher

Fulbright Scholar - Universidade Federal de Goiás, Brasil
PhD - UC Davis Ecology

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Memory issue in R
parts:
I used to use merge a lot and have moved to dplyr for doing the same things using inner_join() and outer_join() mainly because it is a bit faster, not because I'm pushing memory limits like you are. dplyr is based upon data.table and tries hard to not make extra copies of data in RAM when it's not necessary. It sounds like that might be happening with merge() if it is trying to allocate 16 GB of RAM, but your vector is pretty large. 

Can you describe your files a bit more?
Maybe use str() and dim().

Maybe give dplyr a try? 

B
